newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ZAIRE TALKS START BUT NO OBVIOUS WAY TO COMPROMISE.
newsitem.headline: ZAIRE TALKS START BUT NO OBVIOUS WAY TO COMPROMISE.

text.p: Zaire peace negotiations got under way in earnest on Sunday at a secret location in South Africa under a virtual news blackout.
"The talks have started," a South African foreign ministry spokesman said.
Representatives of rebel leader Laurent Kabila and negotiators from the Kinshasa government sat down to open substantive discussions at about 0830 GMT, he added.

A South Africa-based representative of the rebel alliance said the delay between Saturday's formal opening of the peace conference and the start of actual talks was due purely to "organisational matters".
Analysts said it was difficult to predict if the two sides could achieve a compromise that would permit a ceasefire in the six-month-old civil war.
Rebel forces appear to have the run of the country, marching into one town after another meeting no resistance but, instead, only cheers from the people.
They now control more than a third of the country and have vowed to go all the way to Kinshasa to force President Mobutu Sese Seko to step down.
There has been no indication that Mobutu, who has held on to absolute power for 31 years, is getting ready to quit, although he is suffering from prostate cancer and his government is in disarray.

The negotiations, brokered by the United Nations and South Africa, got off to a frosty start in Pretoria on Saturday, with rebel envoy Bizima Karaha in effect telling the government delegation it was now or never if they wanted a peaceful settlement.
